sources.entry: Rust: _Mini-LSM: Build a Database Storage Engine in Rust_

summary.title: Learn Database Internals — Mini-LSM
summary.one_liner: Mini-LSM is a hands-on Rust course in which you build an LSM-tree storage engine covering SSTables, compaction, WAL recovery, MVCC, and transactions.
keywords: how does a database store data
takeaways: LSM trees batch writes into immutable SST files on disk, and a background compaction process merges them to apply updates and deletions.
The course covers the storage layer end to end: in-memory write path, on-disk format, compaction, manifests and WAL recovery, snapshots, MVCC, and concurrency control.
Compaction strategy tunes the tradeoff between read, write, and space amplification for a given workload.
Prerequisites are basic Rust and familiarity with a Bitcask-style log-structured key-value store; the course does not cover SQL, query optimization, replication, or consensus.
summary.summary: Mini-LSM is a free, Rust-based course that teaches database storage internals by having the reader build an LSM-tree storage engine. It is organized into three weeks of seven chapters each: week 1 produces a working engine (storage format, blocks, SSTs, read/write paths), week 2 focuses on compaction and durability, and week 3 covers MVCC and concurrency control. Each chapter includes required tasks, self-test questions, and bonus tasks, and a reference solution plus a checkpoint repository are provided. A separate guided track is offered for readers who use a coding agent, with the reader retaining ownership of key design decisions.
